## Natural history notes

A small lynx spider characterized by its slender body, long spiny legs, and pale tan to greenish-yellow coloration with distinct dark stripes running along the body. In Florida, it is common in fields, prairies, gardens, marsh edges, roadsides, and other open areas with grasses, herbs, and low shrubs. It does not build a prey-capturing web; instead, it actively hunts on vegetation, using its sharp vision, speed, and spiny legs to capture small insects and other arthropods.
